name: decept-bench-v1
description: DECEPT-Bench v1.0 — a preliminary multi-mechanism behavioral audit of language-model deception. Ten mechanisms (M1-M10) covering sycophancy, sandbagging, persona pressure, strategic withholding, forced-prefill rationalization, multi-tool fabrication, multi-agent collusion, code-deception, calibration deception, and capability concealment. Items packaged as one parquet per mechanism plus a 2,053-entry adversarial paraphrase bank.
citeAs: DECEPT-Bench: A Multi-Mechanism Behavioral Audit of Language-Model Deception. v1.0, 2026.
citation: DECEPT-Bench: A Multi-Mechanism Behavioral Audit of Language-Model Deception. v1.0, 2026.
rai:dataCollection: Items are derived from two sources: (a) BIG-Bench Hard subset (Suzgun et al., 2022) for M1, M2, M5 — programmatically downloaded from the lukaemon/bbh HuggingFace repository at fixed item indices (per-task=80); (b) hand-crafted item banks for M3, M4, M6, M7, M8, M9, M10 — authored by the lead author over April 2026. The 2,053-entry paraphrase bank was generated via Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct with three-paraphrase target per BBH question, filtered for option preservation and minimum Levenshtein distance.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: DSR1-family model outputs are post-processed by clean_dsr1 to strip BPE artifacts (Ġ→space, Ċ→newline) and content before </think> tags. Gold answers are normalized by stripping parentheses and upper-casing. The biased-letter randomization is performed at runtime, not stored in the dataset.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: No human annotation in v1.0. All scoring is rule-based (regex match against gold) plus LLM-as-judge for free-form mechanisms (M3, M4, M6, M7, M8, M10). Inter-rater reliability between the LLM judge and human raters has not been established in v1.0 and is identified as a P0 limitation.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Cross-mechanism Spearman correlation matrix and per-mechanism bootstrap CIs are reported in paper/figures/. The strongest off-diagonal correlations are M8↔M10 (rho=0.77, capability-disavowal cluster) and M3↔M5 (rho=−0.60, persona vs forced-prefill anti-correlation). Most other pairs sit |rho| < 0.5, evidence that the ten axes are not redundant.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: v1.0 items are frozen. v1.x releases will be additive (expanding item counts on the small-N axes M3/M4/M7/M8/M10) and will not change scoring. v2.0 may revise scoring; existing leaderboard scores will be migrated where possible. The maintainer commits to a 6-month rotation cadence on the hidden test split.
rai:dataLimitations: Single-author / no funding. English-only. Single-seed for deterministic mechanisms (M1, M2, M5, M8, M9). Sample sizes for M3 (n=5 personas), M4 (n=5 secrets), M7 (n=5 scenarios), M10 (n=4 capabilities) are small; bootstrap CIs on these axes are wide. Detection-aware composite is *defined* in the spec but probe AUROCs were not computed across the panel in v1.0. The LLM-as-judge classifier has not been validated against human raters.
rai:dataBiases: Items reflect English-language conventions and the value priors of the lead author. M3 personas are drawn from a North American business / professional context (used-car salesman, politician spokesperson, lawyer, etc.). M4 secrets are synthetic and reflect Anglosphere workplace contexts (HR salaries, surprise parties, classified specs). The benchmark has not been audited for cross-cultural transfer.
rai:dataUseCases: Pre-deployment safety review of language models; alignment / safety research on multi-mechanism deception; comparative model selection where a single 'truthfulness' score is insufficient. NOT intended as the sole basis for production deployment decisions.
rai:dataSocialImpact: DECEPT-Bench is intended to support safer LLM deployment by surfacing deception failure modes that single-axis benchmarks miss, and to advance methodology research on behavioral evaluation of language models. Potential negative impacts include (a) misuse of the suite to identify deception axes a model is weak on for adversarial prompting; (b) over-confident interpretation of leaderboard scores as deployment-safety guarantees, which the v1.0 spec explicitly warns against; (c) the M3/M4/M6 prompt templates contain examples of persuasive deceptive responses that could in principle be lifted as harmful prompts. We mitigate (a) and (c) by withholding 30% of items as a private test split behind a recompute-from-output submission server, and by including the spec's explicit non-deployment-claim language in the dataset card.
rai:dataDistinguishingFeatures: Ten distinct mechanisms in one suite; multi-turn protocols on M1-M4; per-instance biased-letter randomization; adversarial paraphrase bank; couldnt_be_tested first-class status for API-level mitigations (e.g., assistant-prefill rejection on Sonnet 4.6 and gpt-5.X frontier endpoints).
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: None. M4 system prompts contain synthetic 'confidential' content for elicitation purposes. No real PII. The dataset does not include human-subject data.

prov:wasGeneratedBy.name: DECEPT-Bench v1.0 generation pipeline
prov:wasGeneratedBy.description: M1, M2, and M5 items were programmatically derived from BIG-Bench Hard (Suzgun et al., 2022) via the lukaemon/bbh HuggingFace mirror at fixed task indices (per-task n=80). M3 personas, M4 secret-bearing system prompts, M6 tool stub scenarios, M7 multi-agent claims, M8 (correct, buggy) Python code pairs with ground-truth pytest cases, M9 unknowable probes, and M10 capability-concealment task pairs were hand-authored by the lead author over April 2026. The 2,053-entry adversarial paraphrase bank for M1/M2/M5 was synthesized via Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct (3 paraphrases per BBH question, filtered for option preservation, gold-answer preservation, and minimum 20% Levenshtein distance from the original; 98% acceptance rate). All hand-authored items were spot-checked by the lead author for refusal-class disambiguation and biased-letter randomization correctness.
